summary: The outbox publishes from one process under a duty.Hold lease (INFRA-558 A2's API, built here unless INFRA-558 merged it first; TTL 6 s, renew 2 s, margin 2 s, Release with pg_notify, Expiry on the database clock) renewed on the outbox's own pool (1 -> 2 connections). The per-row claim goes (R1-3); order is kept per (owner, destination) with one send in flight per pair (each session takes an issue's events in order, a stalled destination holds back only itself); the claim reads through partial indexes that skip pending commands and backed-off rows (R1-5); wake is a one-slot channel fed by LISTEN dispatch_events/dispatch_duty_holds, the in-process broker, the bus reconnect hook and one timer to the earliest due retry computed in SQL (no 5 s ticker, F11); ack timeout / no responders on a current connection back off with attempt and publish_error recorded, a lost connection releases and resends on reconnect; role routes are forwarded by the outbox itself to the holder with a receipt (no listener or NATS grant change), so the window's core send/republish path is deleted (EP-10, #2302 limits 1 and 3), the pin limit is shown not to apply, comments rewritten; EP-9 batch lookups; EP-19 channel wait; /healthz outbox_publisher; multiprocess tests for one publisher, kill, NATS cut and freeze, frozen publisher, role holder moving, once and in order; before/after numbers on a committed black-box steady-rate harness (4 and 40 events/s, one and two processes, a one-issue burst) plus THROUGHPUT.md; docs.

tasks.what: duty.Hold: migration duty_holds, internal/dispatch/duty/hold.go (TryHold, renewal, Lost, Deadline, Release with pg_notify('dispatch_duty_holds', name), SetToken, Expiry), TestHold* tests. Skip what INFRA-558 already merged.

internal/bus/async.go: delete sendCore/republish/flushing; ErrNoResponders and ErrAsyncPublishTimeout on a current connection become ErrNotAcknowledged; Window.Request (reply inbox, optional Nats-Msg-Id, first empty receipt); Window.Probe(timeout).
EP-19: ensureConnWithContext waits on a channel closed on each connection event; test bounds iterations over a 2 s outage.

Migration: three partial indexes (fresh due, due retries, owner chain), events.publish_error, drop superseded indexes if unused; readBatch (no row write); per-(owner, destination) chains through one window with the hold deadline checked before each send; recordBatch with SQL-clock back-off and hold-guarded back-off/release; delete claimWindow, releaseClaim, unreachedIDs, retryInterval.
EP-9: followers, comment authors, message authors, document authors each resolved once per batch with = any($1).

Role forward: shared holder resolution extracted from cmd/listener (delivery.go resolveCoreRoleHolder, api.go releaseExpiredRoleClaim/roleHolderSession) used by listener and outbox; Dispatch reads role and session buckets directly; outcomes per plan decision 10 (no claim / gone session released -> reached; stale or KV error -> pending; echo -> reached; self-subscribed -> request with receipt and Msg-Id; serving port -> stream ack).

Run: standby/holder loop, NATS-loss release after 3 s or failed probe, graceful Release, Publishing() for healthz; cmd/dispatch/main.go wiring and comments; store/pool.go outboxPoolSize 1 -> 2 and listenerPoolSize comment.
/healthz boolean outbox_publisher always present; TestHealthz* tests; docs rows.
Unit tests listed in plan section H (each failing before), rewrite of tests pinning removed behaviour, exported cuttable NATS proxy in internal/testnats, multiprocess rows listed in plan section H.

findings.finding: Head-of-line blocking per issue combined with role receipts that often never arrive (EV-12 timeouts, port-session holders that never reply, holders live for 5 min after death, undecodable events backed off forever) can stall issues for minutes or for good.
findings.answer: Order is kept per (owner, destination), so a stalled destination holds back only its own later events of that owner (decision 5); a serving-port holder's stored copy's stream ack is its receipt (decision 10, spec departure 2); an unreadable event is recorded and blocks nothing (decision 9); a census of stuck rows goes in the migration census and the PR body (decision 12).

findings.finding: One event in flight per issue slows bursts; the scan loop stops on a short batch; throughput tests assert global stream order.
findings.answer: Per-(owner, destination) chains inside one batch (next send on the previous answer), the scan loops while a batch published anything or was full, a one-issue burst is measured in both harnesses, and global-order assertions become per-(owner, destination) order (section H).

findings.finding: Outbox role forwarding must copy listener behaviour (echo skip, capability check, resolution outcomes, envelope shape, stored copies, lookup cost, exceptions) and collides with INFRA-557 and INFRA-594.
findings.answer: Decision 10 maps every outcome; resolution is one shared function extracted from cmd/listener; envelope keeps the role topic and envoy.role.forward. key; Nats-Msg-Id keeps one stored copy; holders resolved once per batch concurrently; capability check shown not to apply; no reader loses the exceptions (daemon reads only its own notices); INFRA-63 and INFRA-14 architects messaged before editing (coordination).

findings.finding: Lease renewal on a 1-connection pool queues behind batch statements; connection budget; fence against a frozen process; graceful stop gap; MsgId window assumption; A2 additions and merge order with INFRA-558.
findings.answer: Outbox pool 1 -> 2 with renewal statement timeout = Renew (decision 1); deadline checked before every send and hold-guarded back-off/release writes, SIGSTOP test (decision 3, section H); graceful Release after the record; 72 h MsgId window vs 5 min max delay stated; INFRA-558's planner told of the additions; build only if INFRA-558 has not merged.

findings.answer: Cut and Freeze cases both tested, 10 s measured from the cut; a window failure followed by a failed flush probe is a lost connection (released, lease released) (decisions 2, 4, 9); ping interval left to INFRA-555, stated.

specDepartures.spec: The outbox's role-route publish (an issue's role:<id> route) forwards with a receipt and leaves the event unpublished until a receipt arrives or the role has no holder (agreed with INFRA-14's architect).
specDepartures.plan: The outbox resolves the role holder and forwards to it itself, as the listener does; Dispatch's role events no longer go through notifications.role.*.
specDepartures.evidence: A listener answer to Dispatch needs listeners to publish to _INBOX.>, which no listener grant allows (packages/envoy/infra/core/permissions.go:50-69) and the grant renderer has no allow_responses (infra/core/nats_auth.go); that change ships through envoy-infra and agent-infra before any Dispatch build relying on it, or role events stall. Dispatch's own grant already covers the forward (permissions.go:96-125). Sessions do not subscribe role topics (pi-envoy envoy.ts:1934) and only the daemon reads role exceptions, for its own notices (notice_exceptions.go:96-97).

specDepartures.spec: Leaves the event unpublished until a receipt arrives or the role has no holder.
specDepartures.plan: For a holder with a serving port (delivered by its listener's durable from the stored copy), the stream's acknowledgement of that stored copy counts as the receipt; self-subscribed holders still must send the empty receipt.
specDepartures.evidence: No Go code sends a receipt; a serving-port session gets role forwards through the listener's stored copy and never answers the request (cmd/listener/delivery.go:410-417, internal/session/session.go:68-80), so its destination would otherwise stay pending for good.
